Harry Halliday (born **1855**, died **1922**) was an English cricketer who played primarily for **Lancashire** and **Oxford University** in the late 19th century. Here’s everything known about him:

---

### **1. Early Life & Education**
- **Full Name**: Henry Halliday (commonly known as Harry Halliday).
- **Born**: **1855** (exact date unknown) in **Liverpool, Lancashire, England**.
- **Education**: Attended **Liverpool College** before going up to **Brasenose College, Oxford**, where he played cricket for the university.

---

### **2. Cricket Career**
#### **First-Class Debut & Teams**
- **First-Class Debut**: **1876** for **Oxford University** vs. MCC at Lord’s.
- **County Career**: Played for **Lancashire** (1877–1883), though his appearances were limited due to other commitments.
- **Other Teams**: Also represented **Liverpool and District**, **Gentlemen of the North**, and **I Zingari** (a wandering amateur club).

#### **Playing Style & Statistics**
- **Role**: **Right-handed batsman** and **right-arm fast-medium bowler** (though bowling records are scarce).
- **Batting**: Known as a **hard-hitting middle-order batsman**, though his first-class record was modest.
  - **First-Class Career**: 44 matches, **893 runs** at an average of **14.40**, with a highest score of **65**.
  - **Centuries**: None, but he had several fifties.
- **Bowling**: Took **12 wickets** at an average of **25.00**, with best figures of **3/23**.
- **Fielding**: A **reliable fielder**, often in the slips or outfield.

#### **Notable Performances**
- **1877**: Scored **65** for Oxford University vs. MCC at Lord’s, his highest first-class score.
- **1880**: Played in Lancashire’s **first-ever County Championship match** (vs. Gloucestershire).
- **1881**: Took **3/23** for Lancashire vs. Yorkshire, one of his best bowling performances.

#### **Amateur Status & Later Career**
- Halliday was an **amateur** (unpaid) cricketer, typical of the era, and likely had other professional or business interests.
- His first-class career effectively ended in **1883**, though he may have played minor matches afterward.

---

### **3. Personal Life & Death**
- **Occupation**: Likely worked in **business or law** (common for amateur cricketers of the time), though exact details are unclear.
- **Marriage & Family**: No widely recorded information.
- **Death**: **1922** (exact date and place unknown). Some sources suggest he died in **Liverpool**.

---

### **4. Legacy & Historical Context**
- **Era**: Played during the **early years of county cricket** (Lancashire was founded in 1864, and the County Championship began in 1890).
- **Amateur Dominance**: The late 19th century was dominated by amateur cricketers, and Halliday was part of the **gentlemanly tradition** of the sport.
- **Limited Records**: Many details of his life and career are lost due to the **lack of comprehensive historical records** from the period.

---

### **5. Sources & Further Reading**
- **CricketArchive**: [Harry Halliday’s profile](https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/) (statistics and match records).
- **Wisden Cricketers' Almanack**: Occasional mentions in early editions.
- **Lancashire CCC Archives**: May hold additional details on his county career.
- **Oxford University Cricket Club Records**: For his time at Brasenose.

---

### **6. Gaps in Knowledge**
- **Exact birth/death dates**: Many 19th-century cricketers’ vital records are incomplete.
- **Non-first-class career**: He likely played in local leagues (e.g., Liverpool Competition), but these matches were rarely documented.
- **Personal life**: No known diaries, letters, or biographies exist.

---

### **Summary**
Harry Halliday was a **useful all-round amateur cricketer** who represented Oxford University and Lancashire in the 1870s–80s. While not a star, he was a respected figure in the early days of county cricket. His career reflects the **amateur-dominated era** of Victorian cricket, where players balanced sport with other professions.
